key_concepts: A fault is a break in Earth's crust along which significant movement has occurred.
Faults form from tectonic plate movements that break the ground.
Faults are classified as active or inactive based on movement history.
Active faults have moved within the last 10,000 years and may generate future earthquakes.
Inactive faults do not cut or deform and do not produce earthquakes.
